title: Utility Line Protection Plans Contractor Dispatch Standard
content:
# Contractor Dispatch Standard

Network Management standard for assigning network line contractors on the Bridgewell Utility Line Protection Plans.

## Rule

A line contractor is dispatched only while the plan status is active. The request goes to a network contractor with trade utility line (electrical for an electrical line) whose service ZIP codes include the property ZIP code, preferred before standard, never suspended, emergency-capable for an emergency; ties go to the contractor reference that sorts first alphabetically. The contractor contacts the customer within the plan's routine contact window in hours, or the emergency contact window in hours for an emergency; a missed window leads to re-dispatch. When the plan does not reimburse own-contractor work, work by a contractor the customer hires is never reimbursed. Each assignment carries the next dispatch sequence number starting at 1.

## Selecting the contractor

| Test | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Plan status | active on Bridgewell's record |
| Trade | utility line; electrical for an electrical line |
| Service area | the contractor's service ZIP codes include the property's ZIP code |
| Standing | never a suspended contractor |
| Emergency | an emergency request goes only to an emergency-capable contractor |
| Preference | a preferred contractor before a standard one |
| Tie | the contractor reference that sorts first alphabetically |

*Hypothetical example:* two preferred, emergency-capable utility line contractors serve the property's ZIP code, with references C-204 and B-517. For an emergency request the assignment goes to B-517, which sorts first.

## Contact windows

The contractor contacts the customer within the routine contact window, or the emergency contact window for an emergency. A missed window leads to re-dispatch.

## Assignment numbering

The first assignment on a service request carries dispatch sequence 1; each further assignment on that request carries the next number.

## Own contractors

When the plan does not reimburse own-contractor work, work by a contractor the customer hires is never reimbursed.
